limit.max-file-size.text: #define MAX_FILE_SIZE 4096      /* max chars to read from file for cut */

storage.destination: X server cut buffer zero, exposed as the root window CUT_BUFFER0 property
storage.replacement: XStoreBytes replaces the prior cut-buffer bytes

f_cut.output: the action string bytes followed by exactly one newline byte

f_file.read_operation: one read of at most MAX_FILE_SIZE minus one bytes
f_file.replacement_condition: replace only when the read returns more than zero bytes

f_cutfile.filename_decoding: the first nonempty sequence of non-whitespace bytes parsed by percent-s; remaining bytes are ignored
f_cutfile.read_operation: one read of at most MAX_FILE_SIZE minus one bytes
f_cutfile.replacement_condition: replace only when a filename token exists and the read returns more than zero bytes

filename_expansion.plain: a name not beginning with tilde is duplicated unchanged
filename_expansion.leading_tilde: any leading tilde is removed and HOME, a slash, and the entire remainder are concatenated

legacy_buffer.representation: an explicit byte array and byte length; embedded zero bytes are preserved
legacy_buffer.replacement_rule: construct or read a complete nonempty successful replacement before atomically replacing the prior bytes
legacy_buffer.persistence_rule: foreign clipboard owners and in-process configuration restart do not mutate the legacy bytes

order: atomically replace the compositor legacy bytes
replace the ordinary Wayland CLIPBOARD selection with a compositor-owned source
mirror the exact bytes to Xwayland root CUT_BUFFER0 type STRING when Xwayland is ready
successful_publish.failure_isolation: an unavailable or failed Xwayland mirror never rolls back the legacy bytes or Wayland CLIPBOARD publication
successful_publish.primary_selection: never read, replace, clear, or otherwise mutate PRIMARY

wayland_clipboard.serial: wl_display_next_serial on the compositor display for every compositor-owned publication
wayland_clipboard.send: write the exact stored byte length, retry partial writes and EINTR, stop on permanent write failure, and close the requested file descriptor exactly once
wayland_clipboard.cancellation: when replaced by any owner, the compositor source is canceled and destroyed without freeing or changing the persistent legacy bytes
wayland_clipboard.destruction: source destroy frees each advertised MIME string, the MIME array, source payload snapshot, and source allocation exactly once

xwayland_cut_buffer.property: CUT_BUFFER0 on the Xwayland root window
xwayland_cut_buffer.payload: the exact legacy byte array and byte length
xwayland_cut_buffer.readiness: actions work before Xwayland exists; once Xwayland and its atoms are ready, any nonempty persistent legacy bytes are mirrored before later actions rely on CUT_BUFFER0
xwayland_cut_buffer.connection_loss: preserve the legacy bytes and Wayland CLIPBOARD source for a later Xwayland readiness mirror

cutfile_source_precedence.xwayland_ready: fetch CUT_BUFFER0 and use its first whitespace-delimited filename token; an empty, whitespace-only, unreadable, or invalid property preserves the prior legacy bytes
cutfile_source_precedence.xwayland_unavailable: use the first whitespace-delimited filename token from the persistent internal legacy bytes
cutfile_source_precedence.clipboard_independence: never obtain the filename from the current ordinary CLIPBOARD owner

action_outputs.f.cut: argument bytes followed by exactly one newline byte, including a lone newline for an empty argument
action_outputs.f.file: the first 4095 bytes returned by one successful nonempty file read
action_outputs.f.cutfile: the first 4095 bytes returned by one successful nonempty read of the resolved file

lifecycle.restart: an in-process configuration restart retains the legacy bytes, active compositor-owned clipboard source, seat, Wayland clients, and Xwayland connection
lifecycle.shutdown: destroy any active compositor-owned source, free persistent legacy bytes exactly once, remove listeners, and issue no use-after-free callbacks
lifecycle.ownership_replacement: a newer f.cut, f.file, or f.cutfile publication cancels and destroys the previous source after the seat adopts the new source

requirements.rule: Recognize f.cut and f.file with one string, f.cutfile with none, and caret as the exact f.cut shorthand.
Preserve the exact reference newline, tokenization, leading-tilde, one-read, 4095-byte, and nonempty-success semantics.
Keep compositor-owned length-delimited legacy bytes independent of transient clipboard ownership and preserve them on every failed or empty file action.
Every successful action publishes exact bytes to ordinary Wayland CLIPBOARD with a compositor serial and never changes PRIMARY.
Mirror successful bytes to root CUT_BUFFER0 as format-8 STRING when possible, preserve native success while unavailable, and synchronize persistent bytes when Xwayland becomes ready.
Resolve f.cutfile from Xwayland CUT_BUFFER0 when ready and otherwise from internal legacy bytes, using the first whitespace token and never the clipboard owner.
The compositor data source handles partial writes, EINTR, permanent failure, fd closure, cancellation, and destruction without leaks, double frees, or stale callbacks.
Configuration restart preserves clients, seat, selections, connection, and legacy bytes; shutdown destroys the source and bytes safely.

verification_scenarios.oracle: The three action signatures and caret alias parse exactly; missing or extra action strings are rejected.
f.cut stores argument plus one newline and an empty argument stores a lone newline.
f.file replaces with exactly the first 4095 available bytes and performs no second read.
f.cutfile skips leading whitespace, uses the first token only, expands a leading tilde, and ignores trailing tokens.
f.cut and file actions publish a native CLIPBOARD and persistent bytes while Xwayland is unavailable.
When Xwayland becomes ready, its root CUT_BUFFER0 is format-8 STRING containing the exact preexisting legacy bytes.
One action produces identical length-delimited bytes through native CLIPBOARD, X11 CLIPBOARD conversion, and root CUT_BUFFER0.
An X11 clipboard requestor receives the exact compositor source bytes after a native-target action.
A native Wayland requestor receives the exact compositor source bytes after an Xwayland-target action.
A foreign X client can place a filename and trailing tokens in CUT_BUFFER0; f.cutfile reads the first token and dual-publishes the file bytes.
Without Xwayland, f.cutfile resolves the first filename token from persistent legacy bytes rather than requiring X.
A foreign CLIPBOARD owner cancels the source but neither alters persistent bytes nor becomes the f.cutfile filename source.
An existing PRIMARY owner and payload remain unchanged across every cut-buffer action and error.
Missing, unreadable, empty, and read-error files plus empty or whitespace-only filename sources preserve bytes and selections.
A file larger than 4095 bytes publishes only its first 4095 bytes with no terminator or second read.
A file containing embedded zero bytes is served and mirrored using the explicit byte length without truncation.
Each successful action replaces the clipboard source; old sources are canceled and destroyed and the newest bytes remain readable.
After in-process restart, existing native and Xwayland clients read the same bytes and no selection ownership is lost.
Short writes and EINTR complete, permanent errors stop, and each requested fd and source allocation is released exactly once.
Shutdown with an active source releases listeners, source resources, and legacy bytes without a callback into freed memory.
